summary: I turned the paused TimeoutNow lead into a sharper, source-derived hypothesis on the same code path and submitted a probe for it. The refinement: when a leadership transfer is interrupted while it still has replication to drain, the transfer goroutine's deferError send on the target's triggerDeferErrorCh sits outside any arm on the transfer stop channel, and that channel's only reader — the peer's replication goroutine — exits when the leader steps down; if the leader loses leadership in that window the send has no reader, the outer transfer goroutine then blocks on doneCh before its deferred setLeadershipTransferInProgress(false), and because that deferred call is the only place the flag is cleared while getLeadershipTransferInProgress gates Apply, config changes, restore and GetConfiguration, an interrupted node that is later elected leader would reject every client write with ErrLeadershipTransferInProgress. Registered the hypothesis as an active child question with its discriminator and submitted twelve real-cluster trials (ten interrupted with a 200-entry backlog and a partitioned target plus partitioned leader, two uninterrupted controls) that record the transfer future error, the flag afterwards, whether the node was re-elected, the exact Apply and GetConfiguration errors, and any goroutine left in the transfer path. Native feedback from two local runs, explicitly not retained evidence: my first probe never exercised the mechanism because the target was up to date and the transfer completed before the interruption; the corrected probe did run the drain loop (leader index 202 versus target index 2) and made the transfer time out, yet the flag cleared in all ten interrupted trials with no stranded goroutine — so that suspicion will be carried or refuted by the retained run rather than left as an unrecorded guess. The startup-replay finding and its resolved gap are untouched.
